extracted.intended_audience: DOD/OMB policy makers, military medical facility managers, and ER (Efficiency Review) teams
extracted.subtask_short: DOD efficiency review for medical care
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for applying OMB A-76, Performance Work Statements, and the Department of Defense Efficiency Review (ER) process to the Military Medical Care function, including measurement, team composition, procedural steps, and limitations. Focuses on selecting functions for review, defining performance standards, and assessing feasibility and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output measure suitability and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Output measures used for many functions may actually be inputs or intermediate outputs and therefore are subject to manipulation if tied to resource allocation; accurate and consistent measures of output, whether direct or indirect, are of extremely high priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware that commonly used output measures can misrepresent true output (they may be inputs/intermediate outputs). Extensive analysis and qualification may be required; prioritize measures that are accurate, consistent, and resistant to manipulation. (See: 'output measures used for many, if not most, functions are really inputs or intermediate outputs subject to manipulation... Accurate and consistent measures of output... are of extremely high priority.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on single-factor productivity measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The productivity program has relied on partial or single factor measures such as the labor productivity ratio, which can mislead resource allocation decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use total or partial factor productivity measurement rather than overemphasizing direct labor productivity. Adopt a holistic approach to productivity measurement to inform total resource allocation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures must provide relevant and valid information for management judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: If management's performance is to be judged on concrete evidence, the measure must provide relevant and valid information; identifiable variables of the transformation process must be described in quantitative values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify inputs (e.g., manpower dollars per hour, beds dollars per bed, total resource cost) and outputs (e.g., dollars per patient day, output per unit of input). Recognize critiques that many measures assume homogeneous patients and fail to account for structural/process/technology differences or output quality; such qualifications reduce usability for decisionmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components a better productivity measure must adjust for
rubrics_metrics.description: A better measure must consider or adjust for: (1) arrivals (admissions/outpatient visits) generating workload; (2) patient characteristics affecting resources applied; (3) available resources described in dollar terms; (4) organizational characteristics (structure, policies, style of practice, size, capacity); and (5) making output quantity relatable to quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect the quantity and type of patients (disease distribution) and the respective total cost in resources to produce appropriate goods/services for quantity 'q' outputs at an acceptable level of quality, after adjustment for organizational characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-76 contracting-out decision rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Any 'government commercial or industrial activity ... that could be obtained from a private source...' should be provided by such sources if the services are available, if Federal performance is not mandated, and if in-house performance is not cheaper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying A-76, determine whether the activity is commercial, whether private sources exist, whether federal performance is mandated, and perform cost comparisons before deciding to contract out; note that some DOD health care delivery services may be exempt on request of service surgeons general.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 cost-comparison requirements (Most Efficient Organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons and 'Most Efficient Organization' designs must be based upon: (a) the same scope of work and same level of performance; (b) established 'performance work statements'; (c) standard cost factors; and (d) full costs whenever and wherever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure parity of scope and performance level when comparing in-house to private-sector costs; use established PWS and standardized costing factors and include full costs in comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to develop performance standards and indicators (A-76)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Federal activity must develop, implement, and report performance requirement standards and performance indicators suitable for use equally by the contracting organization and by contractors; organizational commercial activities are to be routinely reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use management review and PWS techniques (per OMB A-76 appendices) to define measurable performance standards and indicators that can be used for in-house performance and contract comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS 'describes what work is to be done without stating how to do it. It identifies standards of performance to be met in measurable terms and defining the allowable variance from those standards.' It sets predefined standards of performance for quantity, quality and timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft PWSs that state requirements in measurable terms and include allowable variances; do not prescribe methods. Ensure PWSs can support both in-house performance measurement and contractor performance evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PWS must include Performance Requirement Summary and Quality Assurance Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD direction requires that an in-house PWS be developed to include a Performance Requirements Summary outlining all performance indicators, standards and accepted quality levels, and that a quality assurance measurement plan be developed and implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a Performance Requirements Summary and a quality assurance measurement plan in every PWS to permit demonstration of how effective and efficient an activity is in meeting performance standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD Efficiency Review implementation and labor-standards update schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft DODI 5010.XX stated that all activities are to be reviewed by end of FY87 and at least once every five years thereafter; labor standards will be updated every three years; resources are to be allocated based on the most recent staffing/labor standards and summarized for PPBS justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan ER cycles and labor-standard updates to meet these schedules; use recent staffing standards to justify resource requirements within Planning, Programming, and Budgeting System (PPBS).

rubrics_metrics.name: ER suitability: well-defined, observable, and measurable tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: ER is most successful in activity areas that are essentially well-defined and where tasks are easy to observe and measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer selecting functional areas for ER where inputs/outputs are identifiable and quantitative; avoid areas with poorly defined products/processes (e.g., many aspects of military medical care).

rubrics_metrics.name: ER team composition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If selected for ER, assemble a team of about 6 to 8 persons: two trained analysts; at least one member representing the respective major claimant; and the rest functionally expert workers who have had related training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure mix of analytical skill, command representation, and functional expertise; examples include training from service functional review courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: ER procedural steps and data-gathering approach
rubrics_metrics.description: General approach: draft the Preliminary Efficiency Review Plan; prepare the ER Performance Work Statement; conduct the ER Functional Analysis; and develop and submit the ER Study Report. Team members should use all available sources of information (regulations, organizational manuals, civilian literature) and conduct site visits as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the sequence of planning, PWS preparation, functional analysis, economic analysis, and final report, leveraging external literature and site observations to inform findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use economic analysis to identify best cost-containment opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: An economic analysis is usually conducted by the ER team to identify specific activities/areas within the functional area offering the best chances for cost-containment savings (e.g., outpatient utilization because of Congressional interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus ER resources on subfunctions with measurable potential savings; justify selection with economic analysis and evidence of over- or under-utilization where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand utilization causation (Donabedian factors) before redesign
rubrics_metrics.description: ER teams should determine why patients seek care; Donabedian's phenomena that indicate service-requiring potential include: people, mortality/survival, morbidity, situations requiring care not classifiable as morbidity/mortality, and health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze patient demographics and causal factors for utilization (e.g., via DEERS) to define legitimate care and appropriate scope of outpatient/inpatient services before proposing access or utilization controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of demographic data systems (DEERS) for planning
rubrics_metrics.description: The Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS) provides demographic data for populations eligible for access to the Uniformed Services Health Care Delivery System and is essential for evaluating utilization causation and resource planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage DEERS or equivalent demographic databases to obtain beneficiary status, age, sex, and other demographics required for meaningful resource planning and utilization analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change-management and political/organizational resistance considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency Reviews usually result in personnel reductions and face political and managerial resistance unless incentives exist; success hinges on support from top down and careful long-term planning/relocation to mitigate union and political interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and plan for personnel/union/political opposition; include incentives, stakeholder engagement, relocation/transition plans, and top-level sponsorship to increase likelihood of implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration requirement with other manpower and CA programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless ER is integrated with service programs developed for manpower requirements determination and the CA program, differing approaches may result in wholly variant manpower figures for the same function and duplicated or inconsistent savings estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate ER with manpower determination processes and CA (Commercial Activities) cost-comparison efforts to avoid conflicting manpower figures and duplicative or inconsistent outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and enforcement mechanisms are lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: Governmental policy makers will want required achievement of planned results, but currently there are no established penalties for failure to meet targeted improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design ER programs with clear accountability measures, performance follow-up, and incentives/penalties where appropriate to ensure that planned productivity improvements are acted upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource and time burden of ER implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance time frames for ER require tremendous manyear resources to implement reviews across all functional areas every five years; OFPP Pamphlet No. 4 is formalized, highly structured, and time and labor intensive; short-term losses may result from these expensive efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether sufficient resources exist to support comprehensive ER cycles; weigh expected savings (often 2–4%) against upfront costs and time commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task pricing requirement and associated burden
rubrics_metrics.description: DODI 5010.XX requires pricing of tasks identified in the PWS in terms of manhours, material, and equipment and formulating an effective mix of staffing patterns; this is poorly defined and would imply procedures similar to CA cost-comparison efforts and be time consuming and expensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify pricing methodologies and scope before undertaking task-pricing; plan for substantial analyst time and possible duplication with CA cost-comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up audit requirements and potential audit cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Enclosure provisions require that follow-up audits be conducted; comprehensive audits similar to those required for CA cost-comparison studies could engender huge costs that may overshadow expected ER savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for follow-up audits and consider whether their costs could outweigh expected gains; explore streamlined auditing approaches where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ER unsuitability for dynamic, poorly defined, or nonquantitative functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Many noncombatant and medical care organizations are extremely dynamic and have poorly defined products that are hard to quantify; ER processes are especially suitable for tasks that are easily defined with identifiable, quantitative inputs and products—military medical treatment facilities often lack such characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid applying ER to highly dynamic or clinically complex functions without first establishing satisfactory measurable outputs and stable baselines; consider alternative improvement strategies for such areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: CA program issues to be addressed when contracting out
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems and issues to address within the CA concept include: job security for Federal workers; quality of services rendered; validity of standard cost-comparison values; who decides exemptions from contracting out; short-term vs. long-term impacts on budget outlays; and political, legislative, and regulatory restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating contracting-out under CA/A-76, explicitly analyze impacts on jobs, service quality, cost-comparison validity, governance of exemptions, budget timing effects, and legal/regulatory constraints; incorporate mitigations where necessary.
